input.title: Contradiction on authorization
input.content:
## Involved claims

- Authorization policy lives in the document's own auth scope as replicated grants, so reducers carry no access-control code — `96758a5d-09e0-47a6-8c91-f4a1a7fd6b04`
- Reducer-level RBAC gates operations on action.context.signer.user.address so access control replicates with the document — `b2987190-d95c-4d89-9075-0716c4eb99fd`

## Why this exists

A `CONTRADICTS` relationship was recorded between these two notes at 2026-09-02T22:08:28.187Z. The vault treats a recorded contradiction as an open question, not a fact to leave implicit: until someone resolves or dissolves this tension, both claims stand and readers should see that they disagree.

## How to close it

- **Resolve** when one claim is correct: say which, and consider `SUPERSEDES` on the winner.
- **Dissolve** when both are right in different scopes: state the boundary in each note's content.
input.description: “Authorization policy lives in the document's own auth scope as replicated grants, so reducers carry no access-control code” contradicts “Reducer-level RBAC gates operations on action.context.signer.user.address so access control replicates with the document”. Opened automatically from a CONTRADICTS link — resolve if one side is right, dissolve if both hold in different contexts.

input.resolution: Dissolved: both hold, in different designs. Reducer-level RBAC bakes the rule into the model (no flags, any logic, but a release to change and the refusal is a stored operation); the auth scope makes the rule replicated data (runtime-changeable, refused at admission, but staged behind feature flags and capped by the policy version). The Cookbook ships them as deliberate counterparts — role-based-auth and document-acl, same outcome, opposite mechanism. The boundary is now stated in both notes.
